title: Arancillo durian (ACC.1497): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Arancillo durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Arancillo durian is a durian variety from BPI Davao (DNCRC). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Arancillo is a registered durian variety, also sold or known as ACC.1497 or NSIC Dr 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Dr 01. BPI DNCRC bred it. Its record notes a yield of 105 fruits.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Arancillo durian is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for ACC.1497 or NSIC Dr 01, this is the same durian. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [durian variety finder](/crop-varieties/durian), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Arancillo was about original tree (20 to 25) Clone (7) years old and about original tree (10 to 12) Clone (8) meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 105 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in August October. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Arancillo weighs about 1560 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is mimosa yellow and firm. Its sweetness measured 21.8 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 38.4 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as August October, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits August and October, annual bearer.
**Fruit:** Ovoid, about 1.56 kg, brownish green, firm, fiberless yellow flesh, sweet and slightly spicy, 21.8 Brix, about 38 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the two most popular Philippine durians and the first with an NSIC number. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Arancillo durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is ACC.1497 the same as Arancillo?
items.a: Yes. ACC.1497 is another name for Arancillo, registered as NSIC 1995 Dr 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 105 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Arancillo?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
